stories.headline: Illinois Governor Signs School Cellphone Ban to Avoid Student Distractions
facts: Title: Illinois Governor Signs School Cellphone Ban to Avoid Student Distractions

_Get stories like this delivered straight to your inbox._[**Sign up for The 74 Newsletter**](https://www.the74million.org/about/newsletters/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=top&utm_id=newsletter)

Students in all Illinois public schools will soon have to abide by rules barring them from using cellphones or other personal electronic communication devices during school hours unless they have been given specific permission to use them.

Although many districts already have similar policies in place, Gov. JB Pritzker signed[legislation](https://ilga.gov/Legislation/PublicActs/View/104-0657)Tuesday that will require all districts to have “bell-to-bell” device bans in place before the start of the 2027-2028 school year.
The goal, Pritzker said, is to eliminate the distractions that cellphones and other devices can create so students and teachers can focus their attention on learning.

stories.headline: They Once Taught About a Hero. Now Faculty Rethink César Chávez Lessons
facts: Title: They Once Taught About a Hero. Now Faculty Rethink César Chávez Lessons

_Get stories like this delivered straight to your inbox._[**Sign up for The 74 Newsletter**](https://www.the74million.org/about/newsletters/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=top&utm_id=newsletter)

The same day The New York Times published its investigation of labor rights leader César Chávez’s alleged actions of sexual abuse, Bakersfield College professor Oliver Rosales was scheduled to teach his class, History of Chicanos in the Southwest. His planned lecture happened to be on the farmworker movement.

But on that day in March, he swapped out a reading on the Delano Grape Strike for [The Times investigation](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/18/us/cesar-chavez-sexual-abuse-allegations-ufw.html), including a testimony by Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers, who revealed that Chávez raped her on two separate occasions. The Times investigation

“Some students used words like ‘shock,’ ‘devastating,’ ‘gut wrenching,’ ‘soul shaking,’” Rosales said. “I was glad that it’d be in that moment with students at that time. I wouldn’t want to be anywhere else in the world, if you will, when that story broke.”
